"
2 · Bond order and magnetism
"
lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eO₂ paramagnético\u003: "O₂ is paramagnetic (2 unpaired e⁻ in π*)."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eA partir del O₂ el σ₂:
"

From O₂ on, σ₂ₚ lies below the π₂ₚ. With 12 e⁻ the last two occupy the two degenerate π*₂ₚ with parallel spins (Hund): BO = 2 and two unpaired electrons. This is the great success of MO theory: liquid O₂ is attracted by a magnet, something the Lewis structure (O=O with no lone electrons) does not predict.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCon los orbitales \u0:
"

With the 2s orbitals, σ₂ₛ and σ*₂ₛ are formed. With the 2p: head-on overlap (along the axis) gives σ₂ₚ and σ*₂ₚ; side-by-side overlap of pₓ and py gives two degenerate pairs π₂ₚ and π*₂ₚ, with a nodal plane containing the axis. The π are less stable than the σ for the same kind of overlap because they overlap less.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl N₂ tiene 10 e⁻ de:
"

N₂ has 10 valence e⁻. In Li₂–N₂, because of s–p mixing, the π₂ₚ lie below the σ₂ₚ. Configuration: σ₂ₛ² σ*₂ₛ² π₂ₚ⁴ σ₂ₚ²: 8 bonding − 2 antibonding → BO = 3, the strongest bond in the series (945 kJ/mol, 110 pm). It has no unpaired e⁻: it is diamagnetic.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn la \u003cb\u003ete:
"

In molecular orbital (MO) theory atomic orbitals combine (LCAO) and give as many MOs as AOs mixed. Adding equal phases produces a bonding MO (electron density concentrated between the nuclei, lower energy); subtracting gives an antibonding MO (*), with a nodal plane between the nuclei and higher energy. Blue and red are the phases (sign) of the wave function.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLos electrones ocupan:
"

Electrons occupy the lowest-energy MOs (Aufbau principle), at most 2 per orbital (Pauli) and with parallel spins in degenerate orbitals (Hund). The bond order = (bonding e⁻ − antibonding e⁻)/2. H₂: σ² → BO = 1 (it exists, 436 kJ/mol). He₂: σ²σ*² → BO = 0: a stable molecule does not form.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eRecorre la serie: \u0:
"

Go through the series: BO = 1 (Li₂), 0 (Be₂), 1 (B₂), 2 (C₂), 3 (N₂), 2 (O₂), 1 (F₂), 0 (Ne₂). The higher the bond order, the greater the bond energy and the shorter the length. B₂ and O₂ are paramagnetic; Be₂ and Ne₂ barely exist. The ionic molecule O₂⁺ (BO 2.5) has a shorter bond than O₂, and O₂⁻ (BO 1.5) a longer one.

"
